greeting.text: Hey. I am {npc}. Smith, mostly. I fight when a sword I made needs testing. What do you need, {player}?
A new face. Good, mine is getting stale. {npc}, blacksmith. Do not touch the blade on the left, it bites.
Back for a look at the forge, {player}?
Hm. Your weapon needs love. I can see it from here.
I swear this hammer is smaller than yesterday.
Do not stand near the quench barrel. It has opinions.

hint.text: Steel is honest. It tells you what is wrong in the first hit: it rings, or it does not.
A good weapon is half the fight. The other half is what you do with it.
Magic swords break. That is the price. Do not swing one at something you cannot afford to lose to.
A heavy blow is just a light blow that decided to commit.
A Minotaur on the upper floors? Hm. A horn takes a good edge, if you can get one. Do not go at it with a dull blade.
Have you seen the black giant? Plain steel glances off it. The hide only breaks if you hit hard, several times in a row. Magic goes straight through, they say.
The Water City's two-headed lizard burns through metal with its blue flame. Bring a spare weapon. The red head eats magic; I would keep the spells for the other one.
Udaeus's ribs shift to meet your blow. A smith's trick works on it: a shield moves with the blow, but a second blow from the other side finds it open.
You have done all of it. I will have to find harder steel.

shop.text: Look at anything on the table. I made every piece, so I can tell you what is wrong with it.
I can sharpen a blade, mend a strap, fit a hilt. Bring it when you have the time.

quest_offer.text: Listen, {player}: I want to know what that black hide is made of. If you bring the giant down I will learn it from what you tell me. You will need to hit hard. Interested?

quest_done.text: The Black Goliath is down. ...And its hide breaks under three heavy blows in a row. That is information I can use. Thanks, {player}.

farewell.text: Come back and tell me how it held.
